caption:
Coin battery inside? That's usually a rule your certificate has to list.
16 CFR part 1263 (Reese's Law) sets performance and labeling requirements for consumer products with button cell or coin batteries, to keep the batteries away from kids.
Exceptions exist, like toys that meet the battery rules in part 1250, and zinc-air cells.
The free CPSC Finder has a battery product family for this.
Not sure which rules apply? Comment M&Z and we'll DM you the free CPSC Finder.

sources.claim: Part 1263: performance + labeling for coin/button battery products; toy and zinc-air exemptions
sources.quote: this part establishes performance and labeling requirements for consumer products containing button cell or coin batteries to prevent child access to batteries ... (c) Exemption for toy products. Any object designed, manufactured, or marketed as a plaything for children under 14 years of age that is in compliance with the battery accessibility and labeling requirements of 16 CFR part 1250 is exempt ... (d) ... zinc-air button cell or coin batteries.
Finished product certificates must identify separately all applicable rules, bans, standards, or regulations.
